title: Demonstrate an understanding of managerial expertise and administrative capabilities

lessons.title: What a manager does
lessons.html:
Managing means getting work done well

A manager is a person who makes sure that work gets done, on time and in the right way, by using people, money, equipment and time well. On a farm the manager may be the farmer, a farm manager or a supervisor in charge of a team.

The four main tasks of management

  1. Planning: deciding what must be done, when and how. For example, planning when to plant maize, how much seed and fertiliser to buy and which tractor to use.
  2. Organising: putting the people, tools and materials in place. The manager decides who will irrigate, who will weed and who will drive the bakkie to town.
  3. Leading: guiding and motivating people. A good leader explains the job clearly, listens to workers and treats everyone fairly.
  4. Controlling: checking that the work is going according to plan and fixing problems. For example, counting the crates picked each day and comparing them with the target.

Skills a good manager needs

  • Technical skills: knowing how the work is done, such as how to set a sprayer or check a pump.
  • People skills: talking clearly, solving arguments and building a team.
  • Thinking skills: solving problems and making good decisions, even under pressure.
  • Time management: doing the most important things first.

Example

The packhouse needs 400 crates of oranges by Friday. The supervisor plans how many pickers are needed, organises ladders, bags and transport, leads the team in the orchard, and checks the count every afternoon. If rain stops picking on Wednesday, the supervisor changes the plan and talks to the manager straight away.

lessons.title: Administration on the farm
lessons.html:
What is administration?

Administration is the paperwork and record-keeping that keeps a business running smoothly. Good administration means information is written down, kept safe and easy to find when it is needed.

Common farm records

RecordWhy it is kept
Time sheets and wage recordsTo pay workers correctly and follow labour law
Stock and store recordsTo know how much feed, seed, fuel and chemicals are on hand
Spray recordsTo show which chemical was used, where, when and by whom
Animal recordsBirths, deaths, treatments and sales of livestock
Vehicle and machine logbooksFuel used, kilometres or hours, and services done
Invoices and receiptsTo track money in and out

Rules for good administration

  • Fill in forms neatly, completely and on the same day.
  • Use the correct date, and sign your name where needed.
  • File documents in a fixed place, for example one file per month.
  • Keep private information, such as ID numbers and wages, confidential.
  • Report missing items or wrong figures to your supervisor.

Communication

Administration also means passing on information. Messages, notices on the board, minutes of meetings and WhatsApp groups help everyone know what is happening. Messages must be clear: who, what, where, when.

Using a computer or phone

Many farms now use computer systems or phone apps to keep records. The same rules apply: enter correct information, save it, and never share your password.

Key points

  • Management means planning, organising, leading and controlling.
  • Managers need technical, people and thinking skills.
  • Administration is keeping clear, correct and safe records.
  • Fill in records on the same day and file them in a fixed place.
  • Keep personal information confidential.
